source_text.Q-1058: CI main flake / defect, HIGH. Property 'any set of row writers is invisible after the boundary, and never rebuilds' in test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs (property ~L1402, failing assertion ~L1430 `assert nonseed_rows(a.schema_name) == []`) fails on some ExUnit seeds. Regression of Q-1042 (PR #2397, edf3e614). Evidence: reproduced locally with `LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs --seed 193355` => 56/57; failing case after 2 successful runs: writers [:groups], via :test; nonseed_rows(a.schema_name) got [{"groups",1}] after recycle_pool! although pool_dirty_report(fx(:a)) said clean. Second occurrence on main 28fcc928, CI run 38235738863, shard 3/3 partition 11, seed 40898. H1 (isolation hole, the worse case): the pool leaves a row in an attached tenant after recycle, so a later test can see another test's writes. H2 (test defect): the property asserts on a.schema_name after a recycle that attached a different slot, so it checks the wrong schema. Acceptance: (1) root cause H1 or H2 with evidence from seeds 193355 and 40898 quoted; (2) if H1: SECURITY-REVIEWER note, the hole fixed, fix shown to hold on the failing sequences; (3) if H2: the assertion checks the schema that holds the writes, decision recorded with reasoning; (4) both seeds added as fixed regression cases of the property; (5) the property passes on the failing seeds and on a fresh sample of seeds across consecutive runs, real output quoted; (6) the property's claim (writers invisible after the boundary, no rebuild) is NOT weakened. Related, not duplicates: ISS-1054 (R1 current_database guard), ISS-1055 (R5 typing), ISS-1056 (V2 depth-2 FK). GH #2406, Q-1058.

result.summary: VERDICT: H2. Test defect; isolation hole H1 ruled out. The property asserts on a.schema_name after a recycle that attached a DIFFERENT slot because the claims map leaked from an aborted iteration. Root chain (reproduced with instrumented copy, seeds 193355 and 40898): (1) write!(:fk_chain) uses fixed PKs (groups 00000000-...-0000000000a1, users ...b1) and the generator can emit :fk_chain twice, so the second write raises 23505 groups_pkey (first failure: writers [:fk_chain,:fk_chain] via :test). (2) the iteration aborts before recycle_pool!/0, so {TenantFixture,:claims} stays {shape_a=>1}. (3) StreamData shrinking re-runs in the same test process: fx(:a) claims k=1 = second declared @a slot (schema 817bbc/a6418b), recycle_pool! clears claims, post-recycle fx(:a) claims k=0 = first slot. nonseed_rows(a.schema_name) then inspects the untouched second slot. Probe output: first=tenant_a6418b.. after_recycle=tenant_4a4c4e.. same=false clean=true rows_first=[{"groups",1}] rows_second=[]. Not an isolation hole: reset is lazy at acquire (INV-P12), and the next acquire of that dirty slot was reported clean?:true with the earlier rows gone (iteration rows did not accumulate). Seed 40898 same first failure; its shrink ends in ArgumentError undeclared slot {shape,2} (claims leaked twice). CI log of run 38235738863 not retrievable (gh: cannot connect to api.github.com); seed 40898 reproduced locally instead. FIX DESIGN (test-only, property claim not weakened): (a) make write!(:fk_chain) repeatable (ids from uniq()/gen_random_uuid) so duplicate writers are legal; (b) first statement of each check-all iteration: TenantFixture.recycle_pool!() so an aborted attempt cannot leak claims, and after the boundary bind again = fx(:a) and assert again.schema_name == a.schema_name before asserting nonseed_rows(a.schema_name) == [] and called_sequences == [] and clean?; (c) fixed regression cases: [:fk_chain,:fk_chain]/:test (seed 193355 and 40898 first failure) and a deterministic test that aborts an attempt mid-iteration then runs [:groups]/:test (shrunk failure of 193355), plus a pool-API assertion that a lazily-dirty slot is clean on next acquire. No lib/ or test/support change needed; optional hardening: none required. Probe was an untracked temp copy of the test file, deleted; throwaway postgres container removed; no tracked file under test/ or lib/ modified. Record: docs/issues/ISS-1058.yaml.
